citation: MIP-9, section 5 (docs/mip/0009-group-conversation.md), and the rules an adversarial review set on kan a_2naAacfIB: the banner holds the message it shows, a reply never reads the group, @muster takes no reply, and a reply that failed keeps its words. Holding a banner while the human writes, and saying what waits behind it, are the implementation's own reading of 'a reply goes to that author whatever arrives since'.
why: The banner is where the human answers agents without leaving their pane. A reply that went to the wrong author, a reply that read somebody else's question away, or a banner that vanished with the human's words in it are each worse than having no banner, and none of them shows up as a crash.

cases.name: a message for the human raises a banner once it is fetched
cases.why: The daemon's notice carries only the newest message's number, so the core fetches that entry and draws nothing until it has it, rather than an empty banner that fills a moment later.

cases.name: the group's next message replaces its banner

cases.name: a banner the human is writing in is not replaced, and says who wrote since
cases.why: A reply goes to the author of the message the human was answering, whatever arrives meanwhile, so the banner keeps that message. The newer one waits behind it and the banner says who wrote it and that it is urgent, so somebody typing is not blind to it.

cases.name: dismissing a banner takes it down and a newer message raises it again
cases.why: Dismissing does not read the group, so it stays unread; the dismissed message does not come back, and the group's next one does.

cases.name: reading the group elsewhere takes its banner down
cases.why: The human read it in another window or from a shell; a banner for what they already read would ask twice.

cases.name: reading the group elsewhere leaves a banner holding a refused reply
cases.why: The words the human wrote are still only in the banner; taking it down would lose them.

cases.name: a banner whose message could not be fetched says what the notice said and takes no reply
cases.why: The human still learns something waits, from whom; but its author is only the notice's guess, so no reply is offered.

cases.name: banners stack newest first and fold past three
cases.why: Three banners is as many as fit beside the panes; the rest fold into a count that opens the oldest, the one that has waited longest.

cases.name: a banner holding a reply is never folded away
cases.why: Newer banners would push it past three, and the words the human was writing would go out of reach with it. It stays among the three, and the newest of the rest fill what is left.

cases.name: a group's next message moves its banner to the top
cases.why: Newest on top is by message, so a group that spoke again is the freshest thing in the stack.

cases.name: notifications for messages turned off raise no banner and take down the idle ones
cases.why: `[notifications] messages = false` and mute take Muster's banner away as they take the operating system's; a banner holding the human's words stays, so nothing they wrote is lost.

cases.name: a long message shows its first lines and says there is more
cases.why: A body runs to 1 MiB; the banner shows the first eight lines and the conversation shows the rest.

cases.name: a daemon detached takes its banners with it
cases.why: A banner whose group is on a daemon the window no longer holds has nowhere to send a reply.

cases.name: a question's banner offers its answers, and picking one fills the reply rather than sending it
cases.why: MIP-9, section 6: answers are buttons under the message, and picking one fills the reply so a note can go with it. Nothing is sent until the human sends.

cases.name: a picked answer starts the reply, with no note needed
cases.why: The reply carries the pick twice: its body starts with the answer, for the agent to read with no new parsing, and the post names the question and the answer, for a view to mark it answered. A pick alone is a whole reply.

cases.name: a picked answer holds the banner as writing does
cases.why: A pick is half of a reply to the message shown, so a newer message waits behind the banner rather than replacing it and taking the pick with it.

cases.name: picking the picked answer again takes it back
cases.why: The answer buttons work alike under a banner and in the conversation, where picking the picked answer again takes it back. The core decides it for both, so neither shell keeps its own copy of the rule.

cases.name: taking a pick back lets the message waiting behind it take the banner
cases.why: With nothing written and nothing picked, the banner holds no reply, so it moves on to the newer message as it would have.

cases.name: a refused reply keeps the answer picked and the note, not the body made from them
cases.why: Section 4 leaves a refused reply's words with the human; with a pick, those are the note and the pick, so the field gets back what the human wrote rather than `Answer: ...` above it.

cases.name: a banner names an agent in a pane by its callsign, and replies to its participant name
cases.why: The conversation calls an agent that never joined under a name by its pane's callsign, `otter`, not its pane id. A banner that said `p2w3r07bsd` for the same agent would be two names for one author (MIP-9, section 1). The reply still goes to the participant name, which is what the daemon addresses.

cases.why: The notice names authors as the daemon does, by participant name. The callsigns an earlier answer gave for the group still name them, so the banner says `otter` here as it did on the message before.

cases.name: a group deleted and made again raises banners from its first message
cases.why: A deleted group's log goes with it, so the same name made again numbers its messages from 1. What the human answered or dismissed in the old group says nothing about the new one; held against it, the new group would raise no banner until its numbers passed the old ones, while Muster in front keeps the operating system's notification away too.

cases.name: a banner whose reply is still being sent cannot be dismissed
cases.why: The reply may yet be refused, or never answered, and the banner is where that outcome shows with the human's words kept to send again. Dismissed meanwhile, the outcome would have nowhere to go.
